From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC Trial - Model selection & evaluation plan

Hi Sophia / Daniel,

Great to meet both of you on the call today — thanks for walking us through Acme Analytics' prioritization workflow and the multilingual support needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Replace current rule-based extraction pipeline for customer feedback with an LLM-backed extraction + categorization flow.
- Data: ~500k historical tickets (English + Spanish ~15%, Portuguese ~5%), short texts (avg 30-60 tokens).
- Success criteria: 1) >= 92% entity extraction F1 on our labeled holdout, 2) average 95% intent classification accuracy, 3) end-to-end latency < 350ms p95 for single-chat inference in your Dedicated environment.

Proposed POC scope & timeline:
- Duration: 4 weeks (kickoff Mon Nov 30)
- Week 1: Ingest sample data, baseline eval, confirm evaluation harness (Acme provides labeled holdout)
- Week 2-3: Model selection, quantization & config tuning, run batch evals (metrics spreadsheet attached)
- Week 4: Final run, handoff documentation & next-step proposal

Model candidates (high level):
- Primary: Llama 2 13B (quantized FP16/INT8) — good balance of quality for extraction tasks and multilingual support with modest cost.
- Fallback / low-latency option: Mistral 7B (optimized quantized) — faster and cheaper, slightly lower accuracy on our extraction evals but useful for burst/scale.
- Embeddings: Use multilingual embedding model (we recommend a 1536-d multilingual model) for clustering & semantic search.

Ownership:
- Redwood: technical setup, model hosting, baseline evaluations, and tuning (Ben will lead).
- Acme: provide labeled holdout + sample data, review evaluation metrics, confirm acceptance criteria (Sophia / Daniel).

Attachments: draft SOW + evaluation metrics template and Redwood model profiles for reference.

Next steps / asks for now:
1) Confirm kickoff week (we proposed Nov 30)
2) Share the labeled holdout (or a sample) by Tue Nov 24 so Ben can begin preparing the eval harness
3) Confirm any additional regulatory or security constraints (e.g., VPC-only, KMS)

I'll loop Ben and Lauren on technical and CS ownership. Happy to adjust based on your timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Hi Sophia — thanks for the great questions. A few technical notes to set expectations and propose a concrete model plan: 

Multilingual quality:
- Llama 2 13B generally performs well on many extraction and classification tasks in Spanish and Portuguese when fine-tuned or instruction-tuned and with a small in-context example set. For entity extraction, we typically see a small drop (~2-5% F1) versus English out of the box.
- If Acme cares about minimizing that gap, options: 1) use Llama 2 13B + light-domain adaptation (few-shot prompt templates + small supervised fine-tune on 500-1k examples) or 2) evaluate a multilingual-specialized model (e.g., XGen or a tuned Mistral variant). Both are feasible within the 4-week window; option 1 is faster.

Latency/capacity assumptions:
- The 350ms p95 target assumes Dedicated capacity with one GPU instance per replica and aggressive batching disabled for single-item latency. We'll size the Dedicated pool for expected concurrency after we see your traffic profile.

Model selection recommendation for the POC (conservative):
- Phase A (Week 1-2): Spin up Llama 2 13B quantized (INT8) as the primary trial model. Run baseline evals on your labeled holdout. If we see >90% F1 overall, run the light domain-adaptation step and re-evaluate.
- Phase B (Week 3): If latency/cost is a concern, test Mistral 7B quantized as a fallback and measure delta vs Llama 13B.
- Embeddings: We'll run multilingual 1536-d embeddings for semantic similarity. If you need retrieval-augmented workflows we can add a small FAISS index for the trial.

Evaluation plan & metrics (summary):
- Primary metrics: entity extraction F1, intent accuracy, false-positive rate for sensitive PII detection (must be <1%), p95 latency, cost per 1k queries.
- We'll populate the attached evaluation-metrics.xlsx with baseline numbers and then update per run.

Next technical asks: please upload a 2k-example labeled holdout (CSV or JSONL) to the shared Drive link by Tue Nov 24. I'll start building the harness once we have that.

On security: Lauren will provide details on Dedicated/Private deployment options and the SSO/KMS capabilities.

Thanks — Ben

Hi Sophia / Daniel — quick note on security and success criteria ownership.

Security / deployment:
- Dedicated is the right call given data isolation needs. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for every inference request. We can enable SSO in advance of the trial for your team; SAML-based SSO is supported. I'll attach our standard Dedicated checklist and evidence pack.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Proposed acceptance for the POC (to be confirmed):
  1) Extraction F1 >= 92% on your labeled holdout after tuning (or a documented plan to reach it)
  2) Intent classification >= 95%
  3) p95 latency < 350ms on Dedicated with single-item inference
  4) No critical security gaps identified in the Dedicated checklist

- Technical lead (Redwood): Ben Carter
